hero.eyebrow: Wasm-sandboxed providers · Cedar-authorized calls · one trace per message
hero.title: A constitution of
hero.lede: Dekopon is an extensible runtime for self-hosted AI agents. Providers are WebAssembly components; the model proposes, a separate broker authorizes and executes; and provider credentials can never reach the model.

constitution.title: A change is judged by which goal it serves.
constitution.intro: Three goals, in priority order; a subsystem that serves none of them is a deletion candidate, however well built.

goals.title: Credentials are unleakable.
goals.body: A model may reference a secret; it cannot read any: secret bytes exist only inside the broker, and the native HTTP engine injects them after the component has built its request.

goals.title: One trace, complete.
goals.body: One W3C trace per message carries the whole run: every prompt, every command word with its arguments, every decision, every HTTP call.

goals.title: Extensible through Wasm providers.
goals.body: New capability arrives as an out-of-tree component with a manifest and command words, executed under exact owner-authored constraints; nothing in this tree grows to add one.

nonGoals.title: Six non-goals
nonGoals.note: An argument for keeping or adding code on any of these grounds is rejected on sight.
items: Idempotency, exactly-once, duplicate-effect defense, automatic retries
Crash durability, reconcilable state, audit tamper-detection
A compromised host, root, or a malicious process in the broker’s trust domain

journey.title: Alice may comment. Merge stays absent.
journey.intro: A synthetic PR-commenter agent, followed from the Slack message to the GitHub comment along one trace.

steps.label: Identify
steps.title: Slack authenticates Alice.
steps.body: The gateway carries a canonical Slack subject across the process boundary. The message can’t name its own principal.

steps.label: Propose
steps.title: The model asks to comment.
steps.body: Its one sandboxed tool turns a familiar gh command into a single narrow capability request.

steps.label: Decide
steps.title: The broker checks every boundary.
steps.body: Cedar decides whether Alice may take this action through this agent. Separate constraints pin the host, the methods, and the ceilings.

steps.label: Execute
steps.title: One fresh provider call runs.
steps.body: A fresh Wasm store gets only the host interfaces it was approved for. The broker’s own HTTP engine adds the token after checking the guest’s headers, and refuses a response that echoes it.

steps.label: Record
steps.title: Everything lands on one trace.
steps.body: The broker writes the Cedar decision and the result as log records on the message’s W3C trace, beside the prompt and the HTTP call. There is no audit file: lose the trace store and you lose the audit.
steps.detail: one W3C trace id · policy ids · policy digest

journey.denied: Still denied: approve, merge, the rest of the GitHub API

security.title: Every control here has a limit.
security.intro: Dekopon doesn’t detect prompt injection or make a model trustworthy. It shrinks what a successful injection can reach.

rows.threat: Prompt injection or a model mistake
rows.control: The model can only propose capabilities that exist by name. The broker authorizes each call from trusted context it built itself.
rows.limit: Nothing here detects prompt injection. And on a persistent route, injected text sticks around for a while.

rows.control: Provider credentials never reach the prompt, the shell, or the Wasm guest. The broker’s own HTTP engine injects a destination-bound value.
rows.limit: Allowlist a host that echoes headers back and the token walks out. Pick your hosts.

rows.control: No OS bash, no inherited environment, no host files. Hosts, methods, and byte ceilings are all fixed before the agent starts.
rows.limit: If something hostile is already running as the broker’s user, you’ve lost. This doesn’t help you there.

rows.control: Identity comes from the authenticated transport and a mapping you wrote. Never from message text.
rows.limit: The local dev subject is caller-supplied. It’s off unless you turn it on, and nothing external vouches for it.

rows.control: Authorization is a Cedar policy file and owner-authored YAML, evaluated by native Rust. No model reviews, scores, or approves another model’s action.
rows.limit: Static rules can’t read intent. Grant a capability and it’s granted; the broker won’t notice that this particular comment was a bad idea.

rows.control: The Cedar decision, the prompt, and the HTTP call all carry one W3C trace id. An operator with the telemetry store can reconstruct the whole run.
rows.limit: The audit is a log record on that trace. Lose the exporter and you lose the audit, and nothing here un-posts a comment.

limits: A compromised gateway can vouch for any subject in its attestor lane
Lose the log exporter, lose the audit

useCases.title: Five providers, five separate repos.
useCases.intro: Each one is a Wasm component with a fixed list of operations. None of them hands the model a general API.

items.label: GitHub
items.title: Comment, approve, and merge are three separate grants.
items.body: Nineteen fixed-shape capabilities across repos, issues, and pull requests. There’s no raw API passthrough, on purpose.
items.detail: External reads and writes · broker-held token

items.label: Wikipedia
items.title: Read Wikipedia without a fetch tool.
items.body: Five read-only operations take the model from a title search to a revision-pinned section. It never gets a generic URL fetcher.
items.detail: Public HTTPS reads · exact language hosts

items.label: Ripgrep
items.title: Real ripgrep, zero host imports.
items.body: Real Rust regex matching over documents you hand it. The paths are labels; the provider never opens a filesystem.

items.label: Python
items.title: Python that can’t reach anything.
items.body: A fresh RustPython interpreter runs one bounded script. No files, no network, no subprocesses.

items.label: SQL
items.title: Turso inside Wasm, storage outside it.
items.body: Turso reaches two logical durable files through one exact storage import. The guest never gets a host path.

closing.title: Start with one capability
closing.body: One capability, one policy, one trace. Let the model explore the rest without handing it the host.
